questions.question: Why is an unconditional GAN usually not enough for tasks like sketch-to-photo or map-to-aerial translation?
options: It can only generate grayscale outputs
It has no way to tie the output to the specific input condition
It always requires paired text prompts
It cannot use convolutional layers
questions.explanation: The lesson's core motivation is that production tasks often require a specific input-output correspondence, not just any plausible sample. An unconditional GAN can make realistic outputs, but it is not constrained to match the given sketch, map, or grayscale image.

questions.question: Why are skip connections generally useful in an encoder-decoder for image-to-image tasks?
options: They preserve low-level structure that should pass from input to output
They force the model to use fewer parameters
They make the discriminator unnecessary
They convert paired training into unpaired training
questions.explanation: Pix2Pix uses a U-Net because many image-to-image tasks share edges, silhouettes, and spatial layout between input and target. Skip connections help those high-frequency details survive the bottleneck instead of being blurred away.

questions.question: What is the main idea behind a PatchGAN discriminator in Pix2Pix?
options: It judges only a single global image score and ignores local detail
It classifies many local patches for realism instead of one whole-image decision
It predicts class labels rather than real versus fake
It removes the generator's need for skip connections
questions.explanation: The lesson says PatchGAN outputs an N×N grid of local real/fake judgments over receptive fields such as roughly 70×70 pixels. This local realism assumption makes the discriminator lighter and often produces sharper textures than a single global score.

questions.question: Why does Pix2Pix combine adversarial loss with an L1 term?
options: Adversarial loss enforces realism while L1 keeps the output faithful to the paired target
L1 is only there to reduce GPU memory usage
The two losses cancel each other out mathematically
It is required so the discriminator can ignore the condition
questions.explanation: In the lesson, adversarial loss pushes outputs to look realistic and sharp, while the L1 term anchors them to the known paired target y. That combination is why Pix2Pix stays both plausible and aligned, rather than drifting to arbitrary but realistic-looking images.

questions.question: When does the lesson say CycleGAN becomes useful instead of Pix2Pix?
options: When you have exact paired examples for every input
When you have no images at all
When you lack paired data and need unpaired translation with cycle consistency
When you want exact log-likelihood evaluation
questions.explanation: Pix2Pix assumes paired (x, y) training data, but CycleGAN is introduced specifically for the unpaired case. It adds cycle-consistency losses so mappings X→Y and Y→X reconstruct the source, letting the model learn translation without one-to-one pairs.
